# J3 — Pin a `RichTextCodec` contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

Rich-text encoding is one of the three real differences between Jira Cloud and Data Center: Cloud's REST v3
requires Atlassian Document Format (a nested JSON document; sending a plain string returns 400), while DC's
REST v2 carries descriptions and comment bodies as plain text / wiki markup. Today ADF is hardwired into the
Cloud path — `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides `fit_text_to_adf_limit` and the decode, and
`adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72`'s `map_fields_to_remote` calls `outbound_fields._load_adf()` inline. PR #120's
answer was to copy that whole method and change the single ADF line, which is the duplication this epic exists
to prevent.

## Approach

Define a `RichTextCodec` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with two operations: `fit_outbound`
(fit a local string to the deployment's rich-text limit, returning the deployment's wire shape) and
`decode_inbound` (turn a wire body into plain text). Provide two implementations — `AdfCodec`, which delegates
to the existing `adapters/jira/adf.py` with no logic change, and `WikiTextCodec`, a character-count fit plus an
identity decode.

The shared `map_fields_to_remote` then takes the codec as a constructor dependency, so exactly one
implementation of the mapping exists and the ADF-vs-wiki difference is a parameter. The same codec is the
dependency J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] injects into the relocated `_sanitize_description`, whose
`fit_text_to_adf_limit` call IS this seam — so if J2 lands first with a minimal `Callable[[str], str]` fit
function as a placeholder, this story widens that placeholder to the full `RichTextCodec` and re-points the
sanitizer at it. Either landing order works; what must not happen is `jira_family/` importing the pinned
`adapters/jira/adf.py` directly. Cloud is constructed with
`AdfCodec` and its behavior is unchanged, proven by J1's pinned oracles [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b].

**Alternative rejected:** a boolean or enum flag (`use_adf=True`) threaded through the mapper. It puts the
branch back inside the shared code, grows a branch per deployment type, and gives the codec no place to own its
own limit constant.

**Alternative rejected:** copying `map_fields_to_remote` per adapter (PR #120). One line differs; the other
thirty drift.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (new) — the Protocol + `WikiTextCodec`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py` — wrapped by `AdfCodec`, logic unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` — the shared mapper takes the codec.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier for each codec (pure transforms) plus a contract test run against BOTH implementations, since the
point of the story is that they are interchangeable behind one Protocol.

- shared contract, parameterized over both codecs: a short string round-trips through
  `fit_outbound` → `decode_inbound` to itself; an over-limit string is fitted to at most the limit and its
  decode is a prefix of the original.
- Cloud-specific: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` produces the same ADF document the current
  `fit_text_to_adf_limit` produces for the same input — asserted against J1's pinned value.
- DC-specific: `WikiTextCodec` truncates at its character limit and marks the truncation; `decode_inbound`
  returns `""` for `None` and passes a string through unchanged.
- contrast case: a non-`str` value is passed through untouched by both codecs rather than coerced, matching the
  current mapper's behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test runs against both `AdfCodec` and `WikiTextCodec` and passes for each
- [ ] `AdfCodec` output for the J1-pinned input equals the J1-pinned expected ADF document
- [ ] `grep -rn '_load_adf\|fit_text_to_adf_limit' src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` shows those names
      reached only from inside `AdfCodec`
- [ ] exactly one definition of `map_fields_to_remote` exists in the tree
